title: CRM and ERP Development in Los Angeles
metaTitle: CRM and ERP Development in Los Angeles | TDM
metaDescription: Custom CRM and ERP systems for Los Angeles importers, apparel firms, consumer brands and service companies: inventory, sales, HR, finance and integrations.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) builds custom CRM and ERP systems for Los Angeles companies, working remotely. We design a CRM around the way your sales team really sells, and ERP modules for inventory, HR, finance and operations, connected to the website, store and accounting software you already use. It suits businesses that have outgrown spreadsheets, which describes many of the trade, apparel and production companies in this region.

sections.heading: Where Los Angeles companies run out of spreadsheet
paragraphs: A large part of the local economy moves physical goods. Importers and wholesalers bring containers through the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, hold stock in warehouses from Vernon and Commerce out to the Inland Empire, and sell to retailers across the country. What is on the water, what has cleared, what did each unit cost once freight and duty were added, and which customer is waiting on it? A shared spreadsheet answers those questions until the second warehouse or the tenth salesperson arrives.

The garment trade downtown has its own version of the problem. One style exists in many sizes and colours, cutting and sewing may be done by outside contractors, and the same stock is promised to wholesale accounts and to the brand's own online store. Consumer brands on the Westside face it from the other direction: orders arrive from a store and from marketplaces, a third-party warehouse ships them, and nobody trusts the stock figure.

sections.heading: What a TDM system covers
paragraphs: We build only the modules you need now, on a structure that lets the next one be added later. Discovery comes first: we map your pipeline stages, approval steps, stock locations and reporting lines before any code is written.
bullets: A CRM shaped to your sales process: leads, accounts, quotes, follow-ups and pipeline stages named the way your team names them.
Inventory across several locations, with purchase orders, receiving, transfers and stock by variant.
HR, finance and operations modules, including roles and approval chains.
Two-way links to your website, e-commerce store, accounting software, email, payment gateways and logistics providers, so nothing is typed twice.
Dashboards that show sales, stock and cash in one view for owners and managers.
Migration from spreadsheets and old software, with records mapped, cleaned, deduplicated and checked against the source.

sections.heading: California details that belong in the design
paragraphs: Software for a California business has to respect a few local rules. The state's consumer privacy law gives people rights over their personal data, so a CRM should make it possible to find everything held about one person and to delete it when required. California's wage and hour rules, including daily overtime and meal and rest breaks, are stricter than in many states, so any time-tracking or HR module must follow the rules your payroll adviser confirms. Sales tax rates also differ between cities within Los Angeles County because of district taxes, which matters for invoicing.
We build to the advice your lawyer and accountant give you, and the rules themselves should be confirmed with them.

sections.heading: Buy or build: an honest test
paragraphs: Buy a standard product when it covers nearly everything you do. Build when your workflow is specific to your trade, or when per-seat fees across a growing team will cost more over a few years than a system you own. Before hiring anyone, ask who owns the code and the data, how the old records will be verified after migration, and what support looks like after launch. We go through that comparison with you before any commitment.

faqs.q: Can a custom ERP be built for a Los Angeles importer or wholesaler?
faqs.a: Yes. Purchase orders, inbound shipments, receiving, multi-warehouse stock, landed cost and customer pricing are common modules, scoped around how your goods move from port to warehouse to customer.

faqs.q: How much does custom CRM or ERP development cost in Los Angeles?
faqs.a: The cost follows the scope: how many modules, how many integrations and how much old data has to be migrated. We give a quote after a free consultation and a discovery session.

faqs.q: How long does a CRM or ERP project take?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements and how many modules are involved. The timeline is agreed in the plan after discovery, and larger systems are released module by module.

faqs.q: Can TDM build our system without visiting our warehouse or office?
faqs.a: Yes. We learn your process through calls, screen shares and sample documents, and confirm it with you in writing before building. Staff test each module remotely.
